reading: Flooding in Nepal has left hydropower workers believed to be trapped in an extensive network of mud-filled tunnels.
Rescuers have resorted to explosives to penetrate the hillside and reach the affected sites.
Engineers have been pumping air underground while the search continues.
The operation is led by Chinese and Nepalese military personnel, with specialists from other countries providing support.
A team managed to enter one tunnel but withdrew without finding anyone there.
An engineer involved in the response described how changes to the landscape had made tunnel entrances difficult to locate.
The disaster has affected both operational hydropower projects and facilities still under construction.
The damaged projects belong to an industry on which Nepal relies heavily for electricity.
Relatives have urged the teams to accelerate the search as their concern grows.
